In forecasting experiments on AR(1) series, people overreact to news, and more so when the series is less persistent. A rational forecaster who must learn the persistence ρ also departs from the truth at any fixed ρ, because its estimate is pulled towards its prior, so a deviation from the full-information forecast is not evidence of a bias. We train causal transformers from scratch on squared error, on AR(1) sequences with ρ drawn from U[0, 1], at {{< var design.n_sizes >}} sizes and {{< var design.n_windows >}} memory lengths, and compare each with the exact Bayes forecaster that has the same prior and window of data (window-Bayes). Window-Bayes is the squared-error optimum, so the question is what finite training reaches. Hypotheses, margins and decision rules were fixed in a self-registered protocol, made public on {{< var meta.public_date >}}, after the runs. H1, that the largest model with the full window is equivalent to Bayes, is {{< var h1.decision >}}: {{< var h1.n_equivalent >}} of {{< var h1.n_total >}} verdicts, two measures at {{< var design.n_rho >}} values of ρ, lie within ±{{< var design.margin.mse >}} percentage point of excess squared error and ±{{< var design.margin.gap >}} of implied-persistence gap. H2: with the window cut to {{< var design.windows_finite >}} observations the largest model is equivalent to window-Bayes at each window, {{< var h2.w4.n_equivalent >}} of {{< var h2.n_total >}} verdicts each. H3, overreaction where the matched Bayesian underreacts (ρ = {{< var design.h3.rho_lo >}} and {{< var design.h3.rho_hi >}}), is {{< var h3.decision >}}: {{< var h3.statement >}}; the largest upper end of a {{< var design.level_pct >}}% interval is {{< var h3.max_hi >}} against a threshold of {{< var design.h3.threshold >}}. The verdicts hold at step {{< var design.steps >}}, when the learning rate reaches zero; at {{< var design.step_mid >}} steps the windowed models are not yet equivalent, and the smallest model misses its benchmarks (both exploratory). Descriptively, with the mean and scale unknown a four-observation Bayesian itself overreacts at high persistence, and the human intervals include its curve from ρ = {{< var overlay.first_rho_incl_w4 >}} upward, so the overlay does not show people overreacting beyond an information-limited Bayesian. One architecture, simulated data.
